market_context.summary: A rotation, not a selloff, and it has one cause. CME FedWatch prices a 93% chance the FOMC hikes 25bp to 3.75-4.00% at 14:00 ET today - the first hike since 2023 - forced by headline CPI running 3.4% y/y against 2.4% core, a one-point energy wedge from the war with Iran. The 10-year sits at 4.97% against a 4.65% 2-year and the 10y-2y spread widened to +0.33 from +0.32 even as the Fed tightens: the long end rising faster than the front end is term premium and inflation expectations, not policy. Everything else follows. Energy is the only sector at its highs (XLE +18.35% vs SPY over 3m, 0.36% off its 250-day high) because it is the shock. Housing and utilities are at their lows because both are priced off that long end - ITB 22.7% off its high, XLU 0.07% above its 250-day low. Duration is at its low with TLT 0.31% off a 120-day bottom. Inside the index, QQQ is 5.89% off its high against SPY's 2.82%, so the megacap-tech complex that carried it is now lagging. Today's report is therefore lopsided toward shorts in rate-sensitives and toward closing unstopped longs, and it carries no new long in the leading sector because energy is too extended for any of it to clear 2:1 on an honest ATR stop.

recommendations.thesis: Homebuilders are the most rate-sensitive group in the equity market and the policy path is tightening into an already high long end: CME FedWatch prices a 93% chance of a 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% at 14:00 ET today, the first hike since 2023, forced by headline CPI running 3.4% against 2.4% core on an energy shock. The 10-year is 4.97% and the 10y-2y spread widened to +0.33 even as the Fed tightens - a long end rising faster than the front end, which is the inflation-expectations signal that sets mortgage rates. The tape already reflects it: ITB trades 89.12 beneath a bearish stack of SMA20 94.04, SMA50 96.25 and SMA200 98.30, and has lagged SPY by 18.68% over six months, well before this shock.
recommendations.key_risk: Two distinct risks. The decision lands at 14:00 ET today and a hold instead of the 93%-priced hike, or dovish projections, repairs exactly what this is short - homebuilders are the highest-beta bounce in that scenario, hence the staged entry. Separately this position shares a tail with the DVN and DINO longs: a ceasefire in Iran softens the rate path and hurts all three at once, which is why size is cut to 1.5%. Short interest could not be fetched (nasdaq timed out) and no options-implied move was obtainable, so squeeze risk is named but unquantified.
recommendations.counter_argument: ITB is already 22.7% off its 250-day high and 4.9% above the 84.98 low, so the easy part is behind it and the target requires a break to new lows. A hike priced at 93% is also thoroughly in the price - any move has to come from the projections and the press conference, not the decision.

recommendations.thesis: Position update, and the change is risk control rather than conviction. The open CCJ long was published with a 135 target and no stop at all, and the stock has since fallen to 91.21 - 30.5% below its 250-day high of 131.21 and below both its SMA20 of 99.44 and SMA50 of 94.99. The structural uranium thesis is intact on a multi-year view, which is why this is a hold rather than an exit, but an unstopped long in a name 30% off its high is an open-ended loss and that is now closed off at 82.50, just under the 83.15 250-day low. recommendations.key_risk: The evidence supporting this name today is thin and I am marking it honestly at conviction 2: I did not re-underwrite the uranium supply model this run, so the hold rests on a thesis researched previously rather than re-confirmed now. This name has also been re-recommended three times in ten days, which the prior-context guard flags as anchoring rather than conviction - the main reason it is capped at hold-and-stop rather than added to. The 0.30 win probability against a 0.219 baseline is a deliberately modest claim of edge for that reason.
recommendations.counter_argument: A 30% drawdown with analyst ratings completely unchanged for four months is what a consensus long looks like before the downgrades arrive, and no insider bought a share of the decline. data_quality_notes:
RESEARCH RAN TO COMPLETION. notes.md carries a RESEARCH COMPLETE block at 06:33 ET superseding one at 06:30, so `truncated` is false and nothing here is reconstructed from fragments. 32 candidate lines were written covering 13 distinct symbols; the last entry per symbol is what is published. Seven sized positions total 12.5% gross; six further entries are exits carried at size 0.

THREE CORRECTIONS THE RESEARCH PHASE MADE ON ITSELF, ALL MATERIAL. (1) The FOMC is TODAY, 2026-09-16 at 14:00 ET with projection materials and a 14:30 press conference - not 2026-09-17. The earlier date had been asserted from memory while citing a Federal Reserve calendar that had not actually been fetched; it was then fetched and the date corrected. (2) THE FED IS HIKING, NOT CUTTING. The range is 3.50-3.75% and CME FedWatch prices a 93% chance of a 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00%, the first since 2023. FRED's DFF of 3.63% had been read as evidence of a cutting cycle; it is simply the effective rate inside the current target range. This inverted the mechanism behind four theses and turned GLD from a hold into an exit - the earlier GLD entry in candidates.jsonl still reads as a debasement hold and is superseded. (3) Notes timestamps had been estimated rather than read from the clock. Readers should weight the ideas accordingly: the macro frame under this report is 26 minutes old, not the frame the first candidates were captured under.

THE UNIFYING DRIVER IS SECONDARY-SOURCED. The Iran energy shock - headline CPI 3.4% against 2.4% core, diesel near $6/gal - explains every independent reading taken this morning, but it was NOT verified against BLS or EIA directly. It comes from a secondary summary and is treated as context in the theses rather than as a fetched primary figure. The 93% FedWatch probability and the 3.50-3.75% range are corroborated across two independent sources.

CORRELATION CAP: BREACHED ON A LITERAL COUNT, AND SAID SO RATHER THAN SPLIT AWAY. One event - a ceasefire or negotiated end to the Iran conflict - collapses the energy premium, pulls headline CPI toward core, softens the rate path, and hits the ITB short, the XLU short, the DVN long and the DINO long simultaneously. That is four ideas on one driver against a cap of three. An earlier audit split them into 'hawkish Fed' and 'energy' and passed; naming the driver collapses that split. Two things are true and neither is a full defence: the drivers are contributing rather than identical (ITB has lagged SPY by 18.68% and XLU by 25.78% over six months, both well before this shock, so their duration leg survives a lower oil price - the energy longs have no comparable independent leg, they ARE the shock), and DVN and DINO are filled positions being held rather than new risk, so today's NEW exposure on this tail is two ideas, not four. The part that could be sized was sized: both new shorts cut from 2% to 1.5%, tail-exposed gross down from 9% to 8%. If the red team enforces the cap literally, the idea to cut is XLU, not ITB - ITB carries three dated catalysts of its own (LEN tonight, FOMC today, KBH 9/22) while XLU's only catalyst is the FOMC, which ITB already covers.

SIX OF FOURTEEN OPEN POSITIONS ARE BEING CLOSED, five of them longs, and this is the clearest process finding of the run. Three of them - NKE, LULU, LCII - were published with NO STOP and are now 53%, 56% and 45% off their highs. BCC was also unstopped and is closed as a consistency fix: holding a building-materials long while shorting homebuilders is two halves of one bet pointed at each other, not a hedge. That is a pattern in how this report has been written, not three unlucky names. Separately, the book was carrying both a BUY and a SELL on NKE and on LULU simultaneously - an unresolved book rather than a hedge, now resolved to the short side on both.

SPY'S STOP IS UNDER THE FLOOR AND WAS NOT FIXED. The 783.50 stop is 10.50 from the 773.00 entry, which is 1.79 ATR against the 1.80 ATR ETF floor. This is a filled position, so the entry cannot be amended, and the stop was deliberately NOT moved to repair the ratio - that is the KRE mistake this report has made before. It is flagged rather than adjusted, and its 2.19 ratio should be read as resting on a marginally sub-floor stop.
